title: Mixtures
competency: Describe and classify mixtures as homogeneous and heterogeneous.

keywords.def: A physical combination of two or more pure substances; each keeps its own properties.
A mixture with the same composition throughout and no visible boundary. Also called a solution.
A mixture with no uniform composition; its parts can be seen.
Another name for a homogeneous mixture, like salt water.

en.text: A mixture is a physical combination of two or more pure substances. Each substance keeps its own properties, because they are mixed, not chemically joined. Salt and sand mixed together are still salt and sand. Soil, cooking oil, ink, milk and air are mixtures.

screens.title: Salt and sand
screens.ask: Hiwot mixes rock salt crystals with sand. Is the salt still salt?
screens.after: Mixing does not change the salt or the sand. Each keeps its own properties.

screens.text: Do you think air is a pure substance or a mixture?
opts: Pure substance: it is one gas
screens.why: Air contains oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and more, physically mixed.

screens.text: In a mixture, each substance keeps its own properties.
screens.why: That is why iron in an iron–sulfur mixture still sticks to a magnet.

screens.text: Which is true for a mixture but NOT for a compound?
opts: Its parts keep their own properties and can be separated physically
It can only be split chemically
screens.ans: Its parts keep their own properties and can be separated physically
screens.why: In a compound the elements are chemically joined and properties change. In a mixture nothing is joined.

en.text: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout and no visible boundary. It is also called a solution, like salt water or air. A heterogeneous mixture is not uniform and its parts can be seen, like soil, blood, milk, or oil and water.

screens.title: Can you see the parts?
screens.ask: Which one has parts you can see?
screens.after: In sand and water you can see the sand. Sugar water and air look the same everywhere.

screens.title: Homogeneous mixtures
paras: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout. It has no visible boundary.
It is also called a solution.
Salt water is the same salt-water mix in every part.
Solutions can be solid, liquid or gas.

screens.title: Table 2.4 Types of homogeneous mixture (solution)
table: Soft drinks such as Pepsi, Mirinda, Coca-Cola

screens.title: Heterogeneous mixtures
paras: A heterogeneous mixture has no uniform composition. It has visible boundaries.
We can see its parts by eye, or with a microscope or magnifying glass.
Examples: sulfur and iron filings, blood, milk, sand and water, muddy water, oil and water, dusty air, soil.

screens.text: Which substance makes a homogeneous mixture with water?
screens.why: Sugar dissolves to form a sugar solution.
Homogeneous: looks the same everywhere. Heterogeneous: parts can be seen.
screens.clue: Are there layers or visible bits?

screens.text: A heterogeneous mixture contains only one phase.
screens.why: It has two or more phases. A homogeneous mixture has one.

screens.text: Pepsi is a homogeneous mixture of which type?
screens.why: Carbon dioxide gas is dissolved in the liquid drink.

opts: Every solution is a homogeneous mixture
screens.ans: Every solution is a homogeneous mixture
screens.why: The book: a homogeneous mixture is also called a solution. Milk is heterogeneous, brass homogeneous, air a mixture.

items.title: I Q1. Classify (a–g)
items.why: Elements have one kind of atom; compounds are elements chemically joined; mixtures are physically mixed.

items.title: I Q1. Classify (h–n)
items.why: Brass, milk and honey are mixtures. Hydrogen and gold are elements. Sugar and benzene are compounds.

items.text: Which of the following is a metallic liquid element at room temperature?
items.why: Mercury is the liquid metal; bromine is a liquid non-metal.

items.text: Substance Y is a hard, lustrous solid which readily conducts heat and electricity. Y is likely to be:
Which substance makes a homogeneous mixture with water?
Which of the following substances is not a mixture?
items.why: Pure water is a single compound.

items.text: Which of these are homogeneous mixtures?
items.why: These are uniform throughout (Table 2.4). Milk and soil are heterogeneous; water and gold are pure.
items.clue: Mixtures that look the same everywhere.

items.text: Which of these are heterogeneous mixtures?
items.why: The book names milk and soil. Bronze, air and ink are homogeneous; ethanol and iron are pure.
items.clue: Mixtures whose parts can be seen.

test.text: A homogeneous mixture is also called a solution.
All of these are heterogeneous mixtures EXCEPT …
Which shows a mixture, not a compound?
opts: Iron filings and sulfur that a magnet can separate
Water made of hydrogen and oxygen
test.ans: Iron filings and sulfur that a magnet can separate
test.why: In a mixture parts keep their properties and separate physically.
